Refine

/rih-FYNE/ · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Refine means to improve something through small, careful changes, especially by removing flaws or impurities

Refine means to improve something through small, careful changes, especially by removing flaws or impurities. After dozens of attempts, the chef continued to refine his signature tomato sauce, adjusting one ingredient at a time until the flavor was exactly right.

Worked Example

Between the first draft and the finished book, the novelist refined her opening chapter eleven times, cutting a slow paragraph here and sharpening a line of description there.

The novelist is not throwing her chapter away and starting over; she keeps the chapter and makes many small, careful improvements to it. That pattern of gradual polishing, removing weak parts and sharpening strong ones, is exactly what refine means.

How Refine Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

polish

polish: improve until smooth and finished

hone

hone: sharpen or perfect a skill

enhance

enhance: raise in quality or value

Antonyms

worsen

worsen: make lower in quality

coarsen

coarsen: make rougher or cruder

How Strong Is It? — tweak → perfect → refine

tweak vs. refine

tweak vs. refine: To tweak something is to make one small, casual adjustment, while to refine it is to keep making careful improvements toward a polished result.

perfect vs. refine

perfect vs. refine: To refine something is to improve it noticeably, while to perfect it is to remove every last flaw until nothing could be better.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: again, thoroughly

Root — fine

Root — fine: pure, finished, of high quality (from Latin finis, an end or limit)

Put it together

Put it together: To refine is literally to make something fine again and again: you keep working it toward a finished, pure state, removing whatever does not belong until only the best version remains.

Use the root in a new word: refinery

Use the root in a new word: refinery: The coastal refinery turns crude oil into gasoline by stripping away its impurities.

Word Choice

Neutral / everyday and technical

Common in phrases like refine a recipe, refine a skill, and refine a process. Do not confuse it with redefine, which means to change what something means rather than to improve it.
